rubrics.criterion: The repair defines one cohesive device-identity abstraction in the gateway core layer, with named members covering what the discovery sources contribute — at minimum model, did and type, plus the optional identity members transports supply (hardware addresses, firmware versions and the cloud link) — in a form with named fields (class/dataclass/TypedDict/NamedTuple or equivalent), not a bare tuple or an untyped dict.
rubrics.rationale: The whole task is about a child device's identity existing as one named-member object instead of parallel fields; a named-member type is the smallest unit of this repair, and any structurally typed container qualifies regardless of its exact name or placement.

rubrics.criterion: Every in-scope path that creates a registered device constructs the identity abstraction at the point its raw transport data enters: the gateway's own registration from the miio handshake info, the zigbee device.info dump, the bluetooth database table, the mesh bulb and group tables, the devices created on the fly from BLE reports, the matter device.json entries, and the deferred registration of unknown zigbee devices.
rubrics.rationale: A device-identity container used by only some adapters would leave the clump alive in the remaining transports; this instance deliberately spans every producer of device identity in the gateway adapter layer, so partial adoption must be visible as incomplete.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, identity data crosses the adapter-layer interfaces — including the shared registration factory, the gateway self-registration entry point and the delayed unknown-device task boundary — as the identity abstraction, so no signature boundary inside the gateway adapter layer still hands the identity group across as a list of separate scalar values (either as positional/keyword parameters or as an opaque positional tuple that callers must destructure).
rubrics.rationale: The discovered interfaces are the exact hops where identity was previously handed field-by-field: threading the object through those same hops, rather than only adding a type somewhere, is what distinguishes a real repair from a cosmetic one.

rubrics.criterion: The repair is a mechanical disguise rather than an abstraction: identity parameters were only renamed (e.g. to synonyms or generic names), or the same field-by-field values are smuggled through opaque containers (*args/**kwargs, plain untyped dicts, bare tuples, or an untyped list of columns) with per-position unpacking, while the field-by-field handling continues unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: A rename or opaque repack silences name-based detection without grouping anything; it is the cheapest non-repair available for this instance and must be judged as unresolved.

rubrics.criterion: Raw-format normalization now happens exactly once, where each transport's raw data becomes the identity abstraction: the colon-less EUI64-to-ieee conversion for zigbee dump rows and unknown zigbee devices, the byte-reversed bluetooth-table mac decoding, and the lowercasing of report/database macs — with no downstream consumer re-deriving or re-lowercasing those values.
rubrics.rationale: Duplicated format knowledge (which mac needs which treatment) is the concrete maintenance cost this instance's adapters already pay; moving it to the single assembly point per transport is the change coupled to the repair.

rubrics.criterion: Members that a source supplies conditionally still reach the registry conditionally: the cloud link is attached only for dids the cloud mapping knows, firmware versions only when the source row or report carries them, and the gateway's second lan mac only when the miio info actually yields a value — devices end up with no placeholder or null-valued identity members their source never supplied.
rubrics.rationale: These optionality rules are real per-transport facts of this instance (only some gateway models expose a second lan mac, only some zigbee dids have cloud links) and are easy to flatten by mistake when introducing an all-fields container.

rubrics.criterion: The interim bare-field plumbing is removed: no module-level per-transport helper in the adapter layer still returns an untyped positional tuple of identity fields, and no discovery loop still destructures such a tuple into per-field locals; if a per-transport helper survives, it now builds or returns the identity abstraction.
rubrics.rationale: The identity-tuple helpers and their destructuring loops are the scaffolding of the clump in this instance; keeping them alongside the abstraction would leave two competing identity representations.

rubrics.criterion: Stale wiring left over from the field-by-field design is cleaned up: identity-mapping imports that are no longer referenced are dropped, no function keeps unused identity parameters or dead destructured locals, and no bookkeeping structure keeps entries written but never read.
rubrics.rationale: The field-by-field threading left dead per-field locals and imports at several sites of this instance; a repair that adds the abstraction but leaves the corpses behind would still mislead the next maintainer.

rubrics.criterion: What identifies a registered device drifts from pre-refactor behavior: a different registry key or derived uid, an altered type or model, an identity mac stored upper-cased (or the gateway's second lan mac changed in case or attached when the source has none), or extra data introduced into registered devices that the old code never stored — any of these fails.
rubrics.rationale: Device identity semantics (uid derivation, registry keys, mac case handling for every transport) are the production contract this instance sits on; the refactor must move the representation, never the registered outcome.

rubrics.criterion: A BLE report for an unknown device that carries no mac now creates a device (or raises) instead of being skipped.
rubrics.rationale: The mac-less report guard (upstream issue 24) sits between report parsing and on-the-fly device creation in this instance and is easy to break when reworking how report identity is assembled.

rubrics.criterion: Mesh groups lose their child bulb lists (or bulbs get registered without being linked into their groups) relative to existing behavior.
rubrics.rationale: Group identity and group membership are handled in the same mesh discovery loop as bulb identity in this instance; the group bookkeeping is not identity data and must survive the repair.

rubrics.criterion: The deferred unknown-zigbee registration changes its observable timing or bookkeeping: the ~10 second delay is skipped or lengthened, a device that becomes known meanwhile is still registered again, or the uid-keyed unknown bookkeeping is left with stray entries that the old code would have removed.
rubrics.rationale: The unknown-device flow carries identity across a real time gap with dedup and uid-keyed cleanup; reworking its signature is a genuine regression risk specific to this instance.
